    header Access-Control-Allow-Headers "Content-Type, Authorization"

name: Manual bans: protect this site
description: Answer 403 to addresses banned in Security. Goes first in a site block.

name: Manual bans: host recovery
description: Shell commands to clear manual bans from the host if you lock yourself out. With a fixed admin bind (tunnel stack), add -e CADDY_ADMIN_ADDRESS=<ip>:2019 to the exec command; that address must be in the bind's origins list. Wildcard-bound stacks need no -e. Copy only.
code:
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yaml stop caddy-console
sudo sh -c ': > /opt/caddy/console/bans-manual.caddy'
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yaml exec caddy sh -c \
  'caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile \
   --address "${CADDY_ADMIN_ADDRESS:-0.0.0.0:2019}"'
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yaml start caddy-console

name: CrowdSec bans: protect this site
description: Answer 403 to addresses CrowdSec decided to ban. Goes first in a site block, or directly after the manual ban import.

name: CrowdSec: log fields for detection
description: Logs the User-Agent and a Basic auth challenge as two top-level access-log fields, so CrowdSec's bad User-Agent and brute-force scenarios work while request and response headers stay out of the log. Put it in each logged site, below the ban imports. Copy only.
